correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the printed three-equation CKD-only subsystem. The determinant \(D=\phi_k\psi-\gamma_h\zeta_k\) expands into a sum of nonnegative terms with strictly positive \(\mu\)-contributions. Solving the equilibrium equations gives a unique equilibrium for every \(\lambda_k\ge0\). The exact characteristic polynomial is \((r+\lambda_k+\mu)[r^2+(\phi_k+\psi)r+D]\), whose roots all have negative real parts, so affine-linearity gives global exponential convergence. At the source's positive \(C_k=1\) parameter the actual \(I_k^*\) is positive and the characteristic polynomial has nonzero constant term, excluding the claimed zero eigenvalue. Symbolic replay from the packaged checker returned VERIFY_OK.

originality.rationale: The source itself states the constant-hazard CKD equations and acknowledges that its CKD-free reference configuration is not an equilibrium for positive \(\lambda_k\), but then claims a \(C_k=1\) threshold and transcritical bifurcation. Exact solution of those same equations gives the opposite structural conclusion. Targeted searches of the published-results database and open literature found no prior statement of this correction, and the closest COVID-19--kidney papers use prevalence-dependent kidney-disease incidence rather than the constant-hazard subsystem.

value.rationale: This is not a cosmetic algebra correction: it removes the source's positive CKD onset threshold and its claimed transcritical bifurcation from the CKD-only submodel. Because \(\lambda_k\) is explicitly described as a noncommunicable exogenous hazard, the corrected structure changes how the model should be interpreted: CKD burden is forced for every positive hazard and rises smoothly and monotonically. The exact global stability and monotonicity formulas provide a complete replacement for the false threshold picture and are directly useful when interpreting or calibrating the CKD component of the coupled model.
